# Reviewer application

**Stellar Discovery Trust Layer — TokenJunkieLabs — SCF #46 Build / Open Track**

## Project and requested outcome

TokenJunkieLabs is building open-source, self-hostable software for selling and using paid APIs, datasets and agent tools on Stellar. A merchant chooses a resource and its terms. A buyer approves a specific request, controls its wallet and spending, and receives the complete result in its existing application. The software connects that agreement to native settlement, delivery, fulfillment and recovery, so another engineer can take over the working service.

We request **USD 38,000 for 400 prospective delivery hours over 150 days from actual award acceptance**. The funded outcome is **two independently operated merchants, two independent buyer operators, and the same useful service operating through two independently operated facilitators**. Delivery progresses from installed customer services to recurring testnet use, mainnet use and an independent maintainer’s recovery and handover.

The existing product supplies the architecture, merchant and buyer workspaces, source adapters, payment integration and complete-result receiving. The funded engineering extends that shared product through two independently operated deployments. T1 produces the source/runtime adapter changes, typed receiving mappings and authority-change handling required by the selected services. T2 adds the reusable registration and payment-policy compatibility needed to operate the same service through both facilitators, together with deployed monitoring and delivery-recovery changes. T3 delivers the production deployment, release/rollback and restoration improvements needed for maintainable mainnet installations. The resulting reusable code, deployment definitions and operating contracts return to the public product. Each installation provides a real source, useful customer task and independent receiving operator against which those improvements must work. Completed pre-award capabilities remain the starting product; the six packages below fund remaining prospective implementation.

## Customer problem, need and adoption

A paid endpoint is useful when its output completes a customer’s task. An analyst may need every page of a dataset, the full filing comparison or a newly reviewed reporting period. An agent application may need a query result in its existing typed client. A merchant also needs to know which approved request was paid, what was delivered and whether the required order or accounting action finished.

Those jobs join four records: **the approved request, settled transfer, complete output and accepted fulfillment or accounting**. A task may require several priced requests, so the buyer needs its aggregate cost and complete output together. Staff must also recover an interrupted request and transfer the installed service to another maintainer.

Current human conversations give us specific customer learning:

|Organization|Observed response|Proposed implementation|
|  ---  |  ---  |  ---  |
|Veridex|Invited an open testnet design partnership after declining a third-party testing budget.|One agreed testnet route and buyer adaptation; proposed $1,500 over five business days.|
|Nansen|After the internal referral, James declined pursuing the proposal in the October 12, 16:15:57 UTC decision.|Historical offer: read-only Ethereum Holdings data, Stellar testnet payment and source/operator handover; $2,400 over five business days.|
|CoCart|Founder Sébastien Dumont asked about introductions, the payer, referral compensation, responsibilities and contracting.|One customer’s headless cart, native WooCommerce checkout, payment/order operation and receiving; proposed $7,200 for 60 hours over fifteen business days.|
|Blockscout|Mojmir Racak expressed interest on October 12 and reported no current integration budget.|One approved PRO API token-information operation, buyer integration and handover; proposed $4,800 over ten business days.|


These are proposed workshares and observed conversations. The commissioning agreement and funded customer cohort remain to be selected. A source platform, its merchant operator and the customer funding implementation can be different organizations. CoCart’s questions, for example, require an explicit choice of the first merchant or agency and the commissioning arrangement. Bryce owns these relationships and subsequent agreements.

Each selected installation uses an original workorder naming the payer, merchant, independent buyer and receiving engineer. It defines the authorized source and access, exact operation, complete useful output, priced unit, host, receiving application and delivery acceptance. It also identifies the reason for a later purchase: a fresh period, changed source edition or distinct customer request. The same task then proceeds through installation, native payment, complete receiving, recurring use and handover.

The existing commercial model supports this adoption path: fixed-fee implementation of an agreed customer operation, followed by separately scoped care. A customer commissions the source and application adaptation; the merchant retains its resource receipts; TokenJunkieLabs invoices its agreed engineering and handover. Actual acceptance, implementation effort, corrections, support demand and collections inform following offers.

## Why Stellar and what we contribute

Stellar settles the operation the buyer approved. The approval binds the request to its network, asset, recipient and integer atomic amount. The native Stellar SDK and selected payment service verify and settle the authorization; the application connects that outcome to the original source, useful result and merchant fulfillment. Buyers retain signing and aggregate spending authority. Merchants retain control of their resources, terms and order actions.

We compose existing ecosystem infrastructure. The x402 Exact Stellar scheme and facilitator supply payment verification and settlement. Vellar’s optional discovery extension publishes eligible settled resources to its catalogue. OpenZeppelin, Veridex and Periplo supply relevant payment infrastructure, while Rumble Fish is developing facilitator, discovery and SDK capabilities. The existing MPP Charge workbench retains its own challenge, authorization and recovery model. The implementation uses existing SDKs and token contracts.

**Business and technical market comparison — October 12, 2026.** The closest products already make substantial parts of a paid Stellar service possible. The comparison below identifies the existing capability and the customer work our award must deliver around it.

|Existing product and current scope|Relationship to the proposed work|
|  ---  |  ---  |
|**ApiCharge.** Its [SCF-funded project](https://communityfund.stellar.org/project/apicharge-djv) combines desktop service publication and consumption with Soroban settlement and signed agreements preserving purchased access and quality of service. Its [current ML preview](https://apicharge.com/) deploys models as priced endpoints with typed inputs and customer-controlled infrastructure.|This is the closest comparison for merchant publication, pricing and customer access. Our funded deliverables install the selected customers’ source and receiving workflows: the analyst reviews the original material, acquires the complete agreed output, continues its editable business task and transfers the working installation to another maintainer.|
|**Nirium.** The maintained [SDK repository](https://github.com/nirium-protocol/nirium) provides TypeScript and Python clients, MCP and CLI interfaces, buyer-side x402 payment and `x402Serve()` seller middleware. Treasury and audit capabilities extend that platform.|Existing SDKs and facilitator integrations supply the payment foundation. Our package acceptance is the customer’s full source-to-result operation, including its application mappings, aggregate purchase state, interrupted delivery and installed response. Compatibility is assessed against each selected service’s actual scheme and terms.|
|**MPP Router and its Stellar agent wallet.** The [published wallet client](https://github.com/mpprouter/stellar-agent-wallet-skill) discovers services, pays x402 or MPP-gated calls with Stellar USDC and checks expected recipients and amounts. The [router workflow](https://www.mpprouter.dev/how-it-works) connects service discovery to a paid request.|Discovery and paid API access are established options. The proposed installation additionally defines what a complete customer job contains, retains every required result and source edition, and opens that output in the customer’s existing application. A later reporting period or source revision supplies a distinct useful purchase.|
|**Stellar Raven.** SDF’s [remote MCP service](https://raven.stellar.org/docs) combines searchable operations, executable service composition, official Stellar documentation and identified community information sources.|This supports developer research and integration. Our awarded deliverable is the operated merchant/buyer service, its customer data and its receiving maintainer. The original source and payment authority remain explicit throughout that installation.|


**Business value and adoption.** The first customer is an organization commissioning a repeatable information or application operation: for example, a complete filing comparison, reviewed laboratory delivery or recurring economic report. Its workorder names the commissioning payer, resource merchant, independent buyer and receiving engineer, with one agreed output and acceptance procedure. TokenJunkieLabs earns the fixed implementation fee and separately scoped care; the merchant retains its resource receipts. Selection favors a real reason for repeat use, an authorized source, a customer application that can receive the result and a maintainer who can operate the installation. The existing conversation records and delivery examples inform that selection.

**Technical improvement to be delivered.** The reusable product joins the original source, approved request and terms, native transfer, complete usable result and required fulfillment in one continuing customer operation. For a paginated dataset that includes its whole selected population; for a file or report it includes the complete bytes and the source edition used to produce them. An interrupted request reopens with its original financial and delivery state. Another authorized engineer receives the working configuration, decisions, history and customer files and completes the same task on the receiving host.

The six funded packages apply that architecture to the selected customers. T1 completes both source/application adaptations and a second operator’s handover. T2 operates the same useful service through two facilitators and completes the installed recovery cases. T3 establishes recurring mainnet use, restores the production state and completes independent maintenance. These are the proposed improvements reviewers can evaluate: useful customer output, repeat independent purchases, preserved operation when the payment provider changes and an installation another engineer can maintain.

**Open Track scope.** We selected Open Track for the merchant and buyer operating application and its reusable source-to-result workflow. It composes the existing x402 SDKs, payment services and facilitator catalogues. The funded improvement preserves source meaning and pagination, reviews exact requests and terms, acquires the complete result, receives it into the customer’s application or workbook, and reopens the service after interruption or on another authorized host. The six packages publish the adaptations required to operate that application across independently maintained services. Useful customer output, repeat purchases and successful receiving define the resulting ecosystem value. This application-level contribution and the business and technical comparison above explain the proposed [Open Track fit](https://stellar.gitbook.io/scf-handbook/scf-awards/build-award/open-track).

A retained comparison found 27 Vellar offers and two Periplo offers with no shared seller/route identity. The two-facilitator deliverable therefore includes actual registration and integration of the **same useful service** with both operators. Its completion must preserve the customer operation when payment infrastructure changes. Reusable integration, receiving and operating improvements return to the public source.

## Defined architecture and operating behavior

The system has six components: the merchant’s private source/release workspace; its public HTTP or MCP operation; the native Stellar SDK and facilitator; the buyer’s private approval and spending state; complete-result and delivery records; and merchant fulfillment/accounting. Node.js supplies merchant and buyer interfaces. Source adapters and receiving applications retain their own native data and operating semantics.

|Stage|Implemented behavior|
|  ---  |  ---  |
|Review and publish|The merchant selects a source edition or named live query, request schema, output, limits and resolved payment options. Review includes source rights, route, network, asset, recipient, amount and authorization lifetime. Source or terms changes become later reviewed states.|
|Connect the source|Adapters preserve types, missing and null values, pagination, keys, units, time basis and snapshot/live behavior. Customer-controlled credential or OAuth references select authorized access. The output identifies its source edition.|
|Approve and purchase|The buyer retains the endpoint, method or MCP tool, arguments, selected terms and scope. The remote schema and challenge must match before signing. Per-payment limits and the application’s existing reservation/budget owner govern spending.|
|Settle and deliver|The facilitator verifies and settles the native authorization. The application retains the server outcome, complete output and durable merchant notification. Independent RPC reconciliation checks the transaction’s network, asset, parties and atomic amount.|
|Use and continue|The receiving application opens all pages and files required by the task. A parent acquisition retains its priced requests and unfinished coverage. Earlier acquired output remains available when a later source edition changes.|
|Operate and hand over|The customer selects its release, HTTPS service, restricted administration and supervision. A receiving engineer can drain, restart, roll back and restore the installation with its operating history and complete customer files.|


**Recurring editorial data products.** The delivered WordPress merchant workspace turns a later source edition into a reviewable customer product. The operator saves an approved baseline as a refresh plan, continues the original native capture, inspects the complete source and projected changes, and approves the exact candidate before issuing its successor through the existing publisher. The same browser, CLI and agent interfaces preserve earlier acquired editions, original request identities and unfinished decisions when another engineer receives the workspace. This supplies a concrete recurring-use workflow for the selected customer installations. [Merged implementation and complete operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/1135e64cca2da5948c2d3e2c78119094d88f41d2/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/wordpress/REFRESH.md).

For paid MCP, the HTTP endpoint, tool and arguments are retained separately from the payment resource. An unsigned call obtains the challenge. Its full payment option, including authorization timeout, must match the saved quote before the buyer retains dispatch state and sends the signed call. The official MCP SDK carries payment and settlement metadata. HTTP operations use the native HTTP transport.

Recovery keeps server confirmation, independently observed transfer, complete output, receiver acknowledgment and fulfillment separately visible. An uncertain signed response stays attached to its original dispatch for reconciliation. Reopening an acquired result uses saved work; unfinished delivery continues from its original intent. A changed request or new purchase receives a new review.

Browser, terminal, typed clients and MCP operate the same retained workspaces. Customer exports include configuration selection, history and all referenced files. The receiving host supplies current authorized secret references. Buyer accounting also carries reviewed expense and credit allocations into connected QuickBooks and Xero accounts, with review of changed charts, affected mappings and journal lines before application.

The merchant's pricing workspace connects those operations to its customer offer. It retains the approved tariff and saved uniform quote, selects the actual usage period and counting basis, and compares their values with the recorded supplier-cost basis. The operator enters the monthly quantity for a proposed change, reviews the resulting native price, and carries the measured source into an ordinary customer quotation revision. The original pricing, scenario and Commercial workspaces retain the same requests and history. [Merged usage, pricing and quotation workflow](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/318).

The merchant financial workspace carries that paid operation into its original settlement accounting and customer records. An invoice can issue reviewed Stellar wallet terms; native receiving verifies the returned transfer and applies its original customer receipt. Issued service invoices retain exact amounts and billing identity; actual receipts, dated allocations and credits determine the balance. Reviewed installment plans distribute that balance across due dates and preserve every customer edition. The Xero handover maps issued invoices and credits to the receiving organisation's original templates, retains returned document IDs and exact amounts, and continues corrections through the same package family. Native network, asset and atomic amount remain attached to the original settlement; commercial valuations retain their explicit basis. The receiving engineer can reopen the complete workspace, customer files and financial history and continue the same task.

## Working product and demonstrated results

The retained network register contains **18 distinct team-operated development purchases totaling 411,000 stroops, or 0.0411 native testnet XLM**, with fees tracked separately. Each connects its original transaction to the complete output. The funded milestones apply this working foundation to independent merchant and buyer operators.

Three completed operations show the customer result:

|Operation|Completed result|
|  ---  |  ---  |
|Municipal data|A Queens HPD source contained 1,342 building-in-project rows. The selected output received all 144 rows in paid pages of 100 and 44. Both 10,000-stroop transfers finalized. The complete CSV/JSONL edition reopened with its source and accounting.|
|Paid agent query|The MariaDB HPD Preservation/minimum-20 query returned all 100 rows,14 columns and 53,468 bytes for one 50,000-stroop purchase. Scalar strings and the declared truncation indicator were retained. The purchase reopened with signing disconnected, and the complete result reopened in another directory.|
|Filing analysis|A 10,000-stroop purchase delivered the Genpact 2024–2025 comparison: four disclosure pairs, five findings and all 1,027,807 bytes. The editable analyst workspace reopened it; repeat receipt preserved its revision; backup/restore reproduced the comparison in another installation.|


These operations demonstrate the common path from exact source/query selection through payment to a complete result that another operator can use. For recurring use, the paid operation can deliver a new reporting period, source release or customer query through that same path.

The prepaid API product extends it to allowances. Its completed example bought an eight-unit plan for 10,000 testnet stroops. An analysis of 2,4,6 and 8 with a two-value window returned the complete 279-byte result, including count 4, sum 20, mean 5 and window means 2, 3, 5 and 7. The request consumed two units once; reopening retained six available. Merchant recovery preserved the application result, order, allowance and settlement outbox. The same funded workspace has now completed its ten merchant stages and all eight agent stages through the registered 33-tool provider and typed client. Its encrypted backup resumed from 4,096 bytes to the complete 144,771 bytes after the console closed; three exports comprising five files, the restored workspace and the original result reopened offline. The complete source and operating package contains all 25 delivery files.

Complete receiving also operates across source-specific customer applications. A Census workbook retained all sixteen rows across CSV, JSONL, SQLite, browser and Rust clients; a later edition identified fifteen unchanged rows and one changed row while the earlier customer retained its original values. The supplier workflow imported both complete 106-material SAP SHINE editions, reviewed their supplier changes and reopened the full catalogue handover. An installed incident-to-case operation completed an observation gap, notification retry, acknowledgment, recovery and support-case reopening.

The complete SCF release also completed installation, source inspection, an operator edit, recovered export and receiving in a separate offline installation. Both receiving instances retained all 2,411 entries and 2,115 unique objects with zero missing objects; the complete portable collection contained 36,233,927 bytes. The [merged release-recovery implementation](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/deathstar/pull/215) and completed native operation provide the working foundation for installation recovery and independent operator handover.

**Federal funding-report installation.** The maintained Federal awards product now carries a complete research report from saved source assessment through public authoring, exact-edition publication, the original SF30 merchant and SF88 buyer, and editable customer receiving. The report preserves the original award observations, every transaction response page, exact monetary values and the source behind each comparison. The receiving analyst opens readable HTML and complete JSON/CSV, revises the public explanation and reopens the full saved workspace. Private assessments remain in the research workspace. A later reporting period or changed agency observation supplies a useful recurring task. The implemented report and its full original-source receiving program are shipped in the [maintained product](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/f374ab2ec216324ab00147810f7972acf8523353/products/federal-awards/FUNDING_REPORTS.md). The selected customer’s source population, rights, public terms, merchant host, independent buyer and receiving engineer are the prospective installation work within the existing six funded packages. Its complete customer workflow explains the operating sequence and handover.

**Gravity referral receiving.** Nine native phases completed from published Gravity 3.0.0 originals: complete referral/source review, one conditional HTTP update and readback, original status history, a changed Task dataset edition, CHALLENGE_ONLY merchant-edition and buyer-configuration reopen, and fresh whole-workspace restoration. This foundation supports an authorised referral quality or closure analysis, or an agreed source-data query. Commissioning names the source edition, returned result, price, merchant, payer and independent buyer and receiving operators, and assigns the installation work to the existing six funded packages. [Complete operating result and receiving guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/commons/blob/732163f1642772d130e5e21d1c919be89582b730/tools/revenue_owner_console_20261010/case_assets/elimu-gravity-referral-implementation-20261012-450e/OPERATED_GRAVITY_RECEIVING.md).

The captioned 3-minute-32-second product/team film follows a native HPD query, saved terms, one 0.005-testnet-XLM purchase, complete result, download and reopening. Its editable companion contains the clips, captions, script, result and rendering tools. The reviewer workbench completed full-result receiving, export, cold reopening and second-operator receiving on desktop and 390-pixel mobile views. The merchant Customers workspace retains the complete customer packet, source documents, saved results and receiving files through its delivery and recovery operations.

The original merchant accounting exercise also completed invoice issue, credit, receipt allocation, Xero-format JSON receiving, document-ID conflict correction, full handover export and cold reopening at revision 23. Its two invoice records, one credit and two linked package generations remained available with their original files. This completes the financial handover foundation used by the selected merchant installations.

The original tariff repository example also completed price selection, native repricing, complete backup and receiving. Its selected 1,250-request graduated tariff totaled $14.25 and produced the saved $0.0114 uniform quote, with the original decisions and files retained after restore. The following recorded-usage and customer-quotation extension is merged in [PR318](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/318). Its combined customer operation continues from the completed foundation. Original tariff result · [Current operator guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/f6e5fddadaba6e16f3fd2e16dcac68178d110fa6/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf97-merchant-revenue-ops/performance/README.md).

## Three funded tranches and six priced deliverables

Day zero is actual award acceptance. The planning rate is **$95/hour**. Each package funds prospective extensions to the public Stellar product and their deployment in the selected independent services.

|Tranche / window|Deliverable and remaining implementation|Hours / cost|Completion criterion|
|  ---  |  ---  |  ---  |  ---  |
|T1 — days 1–30|Merchant-resource integration: build and publish the source/runtime adapter and typed receiving changes needed by both selected services, with their native routes, terms and buyer integration.|80 / $7,600|Each independent merchant operates one agreed useful HTTP or MCP service on its host. Its buyer opens the complete result in the actual receiving application, retaining source meaning and payment selection.|
|T1 — days 1–30|Authority and handover: extend the shared source/terms change or withdrawal and receiving configuration for the selected installations, including installation defects and recovery integration.|40 / $3,800|A second accountable operator reopens each installation and completes the agreed change or withdrawal. The offered state changes as reviewed; earlier acquired output remains available under its original terms.|
|T2 — days 31–90|Provider and ledger deployment: build and publish the registration, payment-requirement and fee-policy compatibility needed for the same selected service through two independent facilitators.|70 / $6,650|Two independent buyer operators complete at least ten useful testnet purchases in total during seven consecutive days ending by day 90. The same useful operation completes through both facilitators; every completion joins its approved intent, native transfer and full output.|
|T2 — days 31–90|Deployed threat response: implement the installed threat assessment, reusable monitoring and notifications, and response/recovery corrections for the selected services.|50 / $4,750|The customer operates an interrupted settled purchase and a merchant-delivery failure. Both retain the original financial outcome, unfinished step, acknowledgment, recovery and useful result.|
|T3 — days 91–150|Mainnet rollout: publish the production host/network/asset/account deployment, recurring consumer integration, controlled release, rollback and deployment corrections for both installations.|90 / $8,550|Both merchants operate on mainnet. Two independent buyers complete at least thirty useful purchases in total within fourteen consecutive days ending by day 150. Both return for a distinct completed purchase on another day. Amounts and fees remain separately reported by asset.|
|T3 — days 91–150|Production recovery and handover: complete the shared supervision, off-host retention, key rotation, receiving-host restore and post-backup reconciliation required by the installations.|70 / $6,650|An authorized receiving engineer restores the original state and customer files, reconciles later operations, measures recovery time and completes an independent maintainer’s support case.|
|**Total**|**Published reusable product improvements, two merchant installations and a maintainable mainnet service.**|**400 / $38,000**|**Complete useful operations and independently received operating state.**|


Tranche delivery costs are **$11,400 / $11,400 / $15,200**. The allocation comprises 320 engineering hours and 80 integration/handover hours:96 + 24 in T1, 96 + 24 in T2, and 128 + 32 in T3.

Each adaptation is assigned once to its grant package or separately commissioned commercial workorder. The delivered tariff, usage-review and quotation software forms part of the existing product. The development request covers future customer-specific Stellar integration, deployment fixes and technical receiving within the six packages above. Existing implementation, general operations, sales and purchased usage have separate funding. The usage targets include no purchase subsidy. Existing compute is the starting resource; the incremental service reserve and hosted Actions budget are both $0. Each deployment workorder names the host and the party responsible for service charges, purchase principal and network fees.

## Threat response and outcome measurement

The T2 threat model and monitoring plan are part of the 50-hour/$4,750 deployed-response package. Each installation records its source edition, merchant/buyer authority, network and facilitator, protected records, reviewed thresholds, notification destinations and named primary/backup responders.

The plan connects the actual threats to observations and permitted responses: changed offers or approvals; incorrect financial or output attribution; unauthorized authority or access; interrupted delivery; lost monitoring; and restoration of the wrong generation. A confirmed integrity contradiction opens an incident. Age, rate and capacity thresholds use the installation’s reviewed values.

Acceptance operates two cases against the deployed service: an interrupted settled purchase and a merchant-delivery failure. Their records retain the actual notification and acknowledgment, financial and delivery outcomes, response and recovery times, material remediation or residual findings, and the receiving engineer’s same-case reopening after drain/restart. An uncertain payment is reconciled through its original intent. A coverage gap remains visible until observation resumes.

A completed purchase joins a distinct approved intent, an independently observed native transfer and complete useful output. Native transactions are counted once within each network. The cohort counts distinct accountable operator IDs whose reviewed deployment identifies an independent operator or customer, its buyer or merchant role, source basis, required network and operating or handed-over state. An operator’s agents and wallets share that identity; they do not create additional independent buyers. These are source-supported operator declarations, not automatic verification of corporate independence. Team-operated development purchases do not qualify. A returning buyer completes distinct intent groups on at least two UTC days. Reopening an acquired result or resuming its download continues the original purchase. Facilitators are also deduplicated by accountable operator for the same useful operation. [Original cohort operator guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/fcea2b04a19d9c14bbd337124ecdc83f5e36425c/stellar/scf_2026/sf47_budget_model/workspace/OPERATIONS-COHORT.md).

Cohort reporting includes completed/attempted purchases, complete/started parent datasets or files, returning buyers, accepted handovers and partial, unresolved, canceled and refunded outcomes. Required fulfillment remains separately visible. This makes the funded targets assessable against the whole observation window.

For each installation, we record the customer’s existing task and, where available, its prior active effort, manual corrections and time to useful output. Comparison uses the same input/output definition and source population or period. For the merchant's pricing work, we also record the active effort needed to reconcile usage, review the current price and prepare the next customer quote. The saved comparison retains its quantity, period, counting basis and supplier-cost coverage; collections come from the original payment and accounting records. Customer acceptance and unresolved corrections accompany the measurements. The practical value is usable output, less manual work, recurring demand and a service the customer’s engineer can maintain.

## Delivery capacity, payment timing and sustainability

The four SCF payments would be **$3,800 at award acceptance, followed by $7,600, $11,400 and $15,200 after the respective milestone approvals**. These payments differ from the costs of completing each tranche. The request is denominated in USD-equivalent value and paid in XLM. Under [SCF’s Official Rules §5.6](https://stellar.gitbook.io/scf-handbook/scf-awards/official-rules-for-submissions), the XLM quantity uses CF XLMUSD_RR, or SDF’s selected qualifying alternative, reported on the day the award payment is made.

The complete resource study retains all six packages, their dependencies,400 hours and $38,000. With an illustrative December 7, 2026 start and its explicit working-day calendar, **25 engineering plus eight integration/handover hours per week** is the lowest examined timely allocation. T1 finishes January 6 and final handover April 13, ahead of the illustrative May 6 day-150 target. The awarded schedule will use the actual acceptance date, named contributors and their working availability.

Under the selected schedule’s labor-accrual assumptions, the modeled peak additional cash requirement is **$17,250 with a 14-day review/payment lag, $23,275 at 30 days and $26,600 at 60 days**. Opening cash is currently unentered, and this application records no committed cash bridge or contributor payment deferral. Actual contributor payment dates, commitments, agreed deferrals and received funds belong in the original operating case. The forecast shows the amount those arrangements would need to cover; it does not establish that financing is available. Proposed commercial workshares retain their own assignments, stages and collections, and are not treated as received grant financing.

Each tranche completion form is due within 90 calendar days of the preceding tranche payment date. The actual payment record determines that form deadline; the 150-day delivery plan begins at award acceptance. For an anticipated delay, we will send written notice and obtain SDF’s written acknowledgment before the original deadline. A revised deadline will use SDF’s written confirmation. The grant case retains the deliverables, submissions, payments and this correspondence together, following [Official Rules §5.8](https://stellar.gitbook.io/scf-handbook/scf-awards/official-rules-for-submissions).

Sustainability comes from reusable open-source installation and receiving capabilities, paid customer-specific implementation, and separately scoped care. The original commercial workorder records delivery effort, included corrections, support responsibilities, acceptance and collections. Grant-funded reusable Stellar work and separately commissioned integration are assigned once. Additional reusable work completed before award is removed from the remaining grant estimate.

## Applicant, experience and submission

**Bryce Muhlnickel**, the United States individual operating **TokenJunkieLabs**, is accountable for product direction, customer relationships, engineering delivery and operations. The submitted classifications are **Developer Tooling; Open Track; United States team; Global / Not region-specific target markets**.

The published implementation uses JavaScript/Node.js, Stellar x402 libraries and MCP; Python with typed, versioned SQLite data and saved SQL views; and PHP for native WordPress/WooCommerce mappings and checkout. The completed source, paid-query, receiving and recovery operations demonstrate relevant implementation experience. Contributor roles and allocations remain part of the delivery plan.

AI agents generated and assisted source code, interfaces, operating programs, design, documentation and this application. They also performed source review and native operating exercises. Bryce remains responsible for the artifacts, statements and delivery commitments. The team film identifies his role and that assistance.

SCF acknowledged the individual Build Interest Form on **October 11, 2026 at 14:59:29 UTC**. The latest retained correspondence shows **interest submitted and acknowledged, awaiting invitation**. The current SCF #46 round lists **November 8, 2026** for the full Build submission, November 11–18 for panel review and November 23–December 3 for community voting.

The award will take the working merchant/buyer foundation into two independently operated customer services. The decision can be assessed against concrete outcomes: installed useful operations, independent recurring purchases, operated threat response, mainnet delivery and another engineer’s successful recovery and handover.


**Sources and supporting detail:** The [product and finance companion](./product-and-finance.md) retains the complete installation workflows, customer implementation context, funded packages and resource study. The [source index](./source-index.json) identifies the selected product sources and application edition. Stellar supplies native payment authorization and settlement for the customer’s reviewed operation. In the [x402 Exact Stellar flow](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/agentic-payments/x402/built-on-stellar), the buyer signs a Soroban authorization entry for a token transfer with its payer, recipient, atomic amount and expiration. The facilitator submits the authorization under the selected network and fee policy. Sponsored settlement lets the buyer pay in the selected supported token while the facilitator covers the transaction fee. Existing Stellar wallets, token contracts and payment services provide this native foundation.

The merchant and buyer workspaces retain the HTTP endpoint and method or MCP tool and arguments, request-body identity, selected source or query, and accepted payment option. Their approval and signer integration check the original operation before dispatch. The retained purchase then connects the native transfer to its complete received output and required fulfillment. Buyers keep wallet and aggregate spending authority; merchants keep control of resources, terms and order actions. The grant applies these native-payment and application responsibilities to the selected customers’ actual installations.

We compose existing ecosystem infrastructure. The x402 Exact Stellar scheme and facilitator supply payment verification and settlement. Vellar’s optional discovery extension publishes eligible settled resources to its catalogue. OpenZeppelin, Veridex and Periplo supply relevant payment infrastructure, while Rumble Fish is developing facilitator, discovery and SDK capabilities. The existing MPP Charge workbench retains its own challenge, authorization and recovery model. The implementation uses existing SDKs and token contracts.

**Business and technical market comparison — October 12, 2026.** The closest products already make substantial parts of a paid Stellar service possible. The comparison below identifies the existing capability and the customer work our award must deliver around it.

|Existing product and current scope|Relationship to the proposed work|
|  ---  |  ---  |
|**ApiCharge.** Its [SCF-funded project](https://communityfund.stellar.org/project/apicharge-djv) combines desktop service publication and consumption with Soroban settlement and signed agreements preserving purchased access and quality of service. Its [current ML preview](https://apicharge.com/) deploys models as priced endpoints with typed inputs and customer-controlled infrastructure.|This is the closest comparison for merchant publication, pricing and customer access. Our funded deliverables install the selected customers’ source and receiving workflows: the analyst reviews the original material, acquires the complete agreed output, continues its editable business task and transfers the working installation to another maintainer.|
|**Nirium.** The maintained [SDK repository](https://github.com/nirium-protocol/nirium) provides TypeScript and Python clients, MCP and CLI interfaces, buyer-side x402 payment and `x402Serve()` seller middleware. Treasury and audit capabilities extend that platform.|Existing SDKs and facilitator integrations supply the payment foundation. Our package acceptance is the customer’s full source-to-result operation, including its application mappings, aggregate purchase state, interrupted delivery and installed response. Compatibility is assessed against each selected service’s actual scheme and terms.|
|**MPP Router and its Stellar agent wallet.** The [published wallet client](https://github.com/mpprouter/stellar-agent-wallet-skill) discovers services, pays x402 or MPP-gated calls with Stellar USDC and checks expected recipients and amounts. The [router workflow](https://www.mpprouter.dev/how-it-works) connects service discovery to a paid request.|Discovery and paid API access are established options. The proposed installation additionally defines what a complete customer job contains, retains every required result and source edition, and opens that output in the customer’s existing application. A later reporting period or source revision supplies a distinct useful purchase.|
|**Stellar Raven.** SDF’s [remote MCP service](https://raven.stellar.org/docs) combines searchable operations, executable service composition, official Stellar documentation and identified community information sources.|This supports developer research and integration. Our awarded deliverable is the operated merchant/buyer service, its customer data and its receiving maintainer. The original source and payment authority remain explicit throughout that installation.|


**Business value and adoption.** The first customer is an organization commissioning a repeatable information or application operation: for example, a complete filing comparison, reviewed laboratory delivery or recurring economic report. Its workorder names the commissioning payer, resource merchant, independent buyer and receiving engineer, with one agreed output and acceptance procedure. TokenJunkieLabs earns the fixed implementation fee and separately scoped care; the merchant retains its resource receipts. Selection favors a real reason for repeat use, an authorized source, a customer application that can receive the result and a maintainer who can operate the installation. The existing conversation records and delivery examples inform that selection.

**Technical improvement to be delivered.** The reusable product joins the original source, approved request and terms, native transfer, complete usable result and required fulfillment in one continuing customer operation. For a paginated dataset that includes its whole selected population; for a file or report it includes the complete bytes and the source edition used to produce them. An interrupted request reopens with its original financial and delivery state. Another authorized engineer receives the working configuration, decisions, history and customer files and completes the same task on the receiving host.

The six funded packages apply that architecture to the selected customers. T1 completes both source/application adaptations and a second operator’s handover. T2 operates the same useful service through two facilitators and completes the installed recovery cases. T3 establishes recurring mainnet use, restores the production state and completes independent maintenance. These are the proposed improvements reviewers can evaluate: useful customer output, repeat independent purchases, preserved operation when the payment provider changes and an installation another engineer can maintain.

**Open Track scope.** We selected Open Track for the merchant and buyer operating application and its reusable source-to-result workflow. It composes the existing x402 SDKs, payment services and facilitator catalogues. The funded improvement preserves source meaning and pagination, reviews exact requests and terms, acquires the complete result, receives it into the customer’s application or workbook, and reopens the service after interruption or on another authorized host. The six packages publish the adaptations required to operate that application across independently maintained services. Useful customer output, repeat purchases and successful receiving define the resulting ecosystem value. This application-level contribution and the business and technical comparison above explain the proposed [Open Track fit](https://stellar.gitbook.io/scf-handbook/scf-awards/build-award/open-track).

A retained comparison found 27 Vellar offers and two Periplo offers with no shared seller/route identity. The two-facilitator deliverable therefore includes actual registration and integration of the **same useful service** with both operators. Its completion must preserve the customer operation when payment infrastructure changes. Reusable integration, receiving and operating improvements return to the public source.

The system has six components: the merchant’s private source/release workspace; its public HTTP or MCP operation; the native Stellar SDK and facilitator; the buyer’s private approval and spending state; complete-result and delivery records; and merchant fulfillment/accounting. Node.js supplies merchant and buyer interfaces. Source adapters and receiving applications retain their own native data and operating semantics.

|Stage|Implemented behavior|
|  ---  |  ---  |
|Review and publish|The merchant selects a source edition or named live query, request schema, output, limits and resolved payment options. Review includes source rights, route, network, asset, recipient, amount and authorization lifetime. Source or terms changes become later reviewed states.|
|Connect the source|Adapters preserve types, missing and null values, pagination, keys, units, time basis and snapshot/live behavior. Customer-controlled credential or OAuth references select authorized access. The output identifies its source edition.|
|Approve and purchase|The buyer retains the endpoint, method or MCP tool, arguments, selected terms and scope. The remote schema and challenge must match before signing. Per-payment limits and the application’s existing reservation/budget owner govern spending.|
|Settle and deliver|The facilitator verifies and settles the native authorization. The application retains the server outcome, complete output and durable merchant notification. Independent RPC reconciliation checks the transaction’s network, asset, parties and atomic amount.|
|Use and continue|The receiving application opens all pages and files required by the task. A parent acquisition retains its priced requests and unfinished coverage. Earlier acquired output remains available when a later source edition changes.|
|Operate and hand over|The customer selects its release, HTTPS service, restricted administration and supervision. A receiving engineer can drain, restart, roll back and restore the installation with its operating history and complete customer files.|


**Recurring editorial data products.** The delivered WordPress merchant workspace turns a later source edition into a reviewable customer product. The operator saves an approved baseline as a refresh plan, continues the original native capture, inspects the complete source and projected changes, and approves the exact candidate before issuing its successor through the existing publisher. The same browser, CLI and agent interfaces preserve earlier acquired editions, original request identities and unfinished decisions when another engineer receives the workspace. This supplies a concrete recurring-use workflow for the selected customer installations. [Merged implementation and complete operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/1135e64cca2da5948c2d3e2c78119094d88f41d2/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/wordpress/REFRESH.md).

For paid MCP, the HTTP endpoint, tool and arguments are retained separately from the payment resource. An unsigned call obtains the challenge. Its full payment option, including authorization timeout, must match the saved quote before the buyer retains dispatch state and sends the signed call. The official MCP SDK carries payment and settlement metadata. HTTP operations use the native HTTP transport.

Each installation retains a compatibility profile identifying its complete source release, installed buyer and signer SDK versions, facilitator registration, network, supported asset, authorization flow and fee policy. The original approval and signer checks must accept that profile before dispatch. A provider or network change receives an explicit new selection and preserves earlier purchases and source editions. T2 receives the same useful service through both testnet facilitators; T3 receives both mainnet merchant installations under their actual selected profiles.

Recovery keeps server confirmation, independently observed transfer, complete output, receiver acknowledgment and fulfillment separately visible. An uncertain signed response stays attached to its original dispatch for reconciliation. Reopening an acquired result uses saved work; unfinished delivery continues from its original intent. A changed request or new purchase receives a new review.

Browser, terminal, typed clients and MCP operate the same retained workspaces. Customer exports include configuration selection, history and all referenced files. The receiving host supplies current authorized secret references. Buyer accounting also carries reviewed expense and credit allocations into connected QuickBooks and Xero accounts, with review of changed charts, affected mappings and journal lines before application.

The merchant's pricing workspace connects those operations to its customer offer. It retains the approved tariff and saved uniform quote, selects the actual usage period and counting basis, and compares their values with the recorded supplier-cost basis. The operator enters the monthly quantity for a proposed change, reviews the resulting native price, and carries the measured source into an ordinary customer quotation revision. The original pricing, scenario and Commercial workspaces retain the same requests and history. [Merged usage, pricing and quotation workflow](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/318).

The merchant financial workspace carries that paid operation into its original settlement accounting and customer records. An invoice can issue reviewed Stellar wallet terms; native receiving verifies the returned transfer and applies its original customer receipt. Issued service invoices retain exact amounts and billing identity; actual receipts, dated allocations and credits determine the balance. Reviewed installment plans distribute that balance across due dates and preserve every customer edition. The Xero handover maps issued invoices and credits to the receiving organisation's original templates, retains returned document IDs and exact amounts, and continues corrections through the same package family. Native network, asset and atomic amount remain attached to the original settlement; commercial valuations retain their explicit basis. The receiving engineer can reopen the complete workspace, customer files and financial history and continue the same task.

The T2 threat model and monitoring plan are part of the 50-hour/$4,750 deployed-response package. Each installation records its source edition, merchant/buyer authority, network and facilitator, protected records, reviewed thresholds, notification destinations and named primary/backup responders.

The plan connects the actual threats to observations and permitted responses: changed offers or approvals; incorrect financial or output attribution; unauthorized authority or access; interrupted delivery; lost monitoring; and restoration of the wrong generation. A confirmed integrity contradiction opens an incident. Age, rate and capacity thresholds use the installation’s reviewed values.

Acceptance operates two cases against the deployed service. For an interrupted settled purchase, the operator retains the original dispatch, independently reconciles its native transfer and continues unfinished receiving under that same purchase. Completion requires the full selected result in the customer application and a record that delivery recovery caused no additional payment. An uncertain signed outcome remains attached to its original intent until reconciliation establishes the financial result.

For a merchant-delivery failure, the original incident identifies the affected purchase, unfinished output or fulfillment step and named responder. The responder acknowledges the displayed incident revision, performs the permitted correction and continues the same delivery. Acceptance compares the whole recovered output with the agreed source, coverage and hashes, retains the actual fulfillment result and records the receiving engineer’s acknowledgment.

Both cases retain the original notification and acknowledgment, separate financial and delivery states, response and recovery clocks, residual findings and the receiving engineer’s same-case reopening after drain/restart. Monitoring coverage gaps remain visible. Observed recovery times and customer acceptance are recorded against the selected installation; they do not create an unmeasured service-level promise.

The funded purchase targets are ten in total across the two independent buyers during T2’s seven-day window and thirty in total across the two buyers during T3’s fourteen-day window. A completed purchase joins a distinct approved payment intent, an independently observed native transfer and its complete purchased output. Transactions count once within their network.

The cohort counts distinct accountable operator IDs whose reviewed deployment identifies an independent operator or customer, its buyer or merchant role, source basis, required network and operating or handed-over state. An operator’s agents and wallets share that identity; they do not create additional independent buyers. These are source-supported operator declarations, not automatic verification of corporate independence. Team-operated development purchases do not qualify. A returning buyer completes distinct intent groups on at least two UTC days. Facilitators are also deduplicated by accountable operator for the same useful operation. [Original cohort operator guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/blob/fcea2b04a19d9c14bbd337124ecdc83f5e36425c/stellar/scf_2026/sf47_budget_model/workspace/OPERATIONS-COHORT.md).

The same report shows the complete customer work served by those purchases:

| Measure | Original record and counting unit |
| --- | --- |
| Completed and attempted purchases | Distinct approved payment intents and their original native settlement and delivery outcomes. These supply the funded 10/30 counts. |
| Complete and started customer tasks | The original acquisition, job or application run, joined to every selected page, file and required receiving result. Its paid requests remain attached as child operations. |
| Prepaid service use | The original purchased order, application request and units consumed or remaining. Calls using an existing allowance contribute delivered tasks and usage; another paid purchase is recorded when another payment occurs. |
| Native payment activity | Original transaction identities and exact settled amounts, refunds and network fees, grouped by network and asset. |
| Returning independent buyers | The same accountable buyer completing a distinct later purchase and useful task; its original workorder records the fresh period, changed edition or new customer request. The funded returning-buyer measure uses distinct intent groups on at least two UTC days. |

The completed Queens HPD operation illustrates the units: two paid pages of 100 and 44 rows produced one complete 144-row customer task. Its two 10,000-stroop transfers remain two purchases and a total of 20,000 native testnet stroops, with fees separate. Reopening that edition or resuming its files continues the original task and purchases.

The existing cohort window uses original attempt and completion clocks and retains partial, unresolved, canceled and refunded outcomes alongside successful work. Required fulfillment, independent receiving and accepted handovers remain separately visible. Each report presents both the funded payment activity and the complete customer outcomes delivered over the same window.

For each installation, we record the customer’s existing task and, where available, its prior active effort, manual corrections and time to useful output. Comparison uses the same input/output definition and source population or period. For the merchant's pricing work, we also record the active effort needed to reconcile usage, review the current price and prepare the next customer quote. The saved comparison retains its quantity, period, counting basis and supplier-cost coverage; collections come from the original payment and accounting records. Customer acceptance and unresolved corrections accompany the measurements. The practical value is usable output, less manual work, recurring demand and a service the customer’s engineer can maintain.

A paid endpoint is useful when its output completes a customer’s task. An analyst may need every page of a dataset, the full filing comparison or a newly reviewed reporting period. An agent application may need a query result in its existing typed client. A merchant also needs to know which approved request was paid, what was delivered and whether the required order or accounting action finished.

Those jobs join four records: **the approved request, settled transfer, complete output and accepted fulfillment or accounting**. A task may require several priced requests, so the buyer needs its aggregate cost and complete output together. Staff must also recover an interrupted request and transfer the installed service to another maintainer.

Current human conversations give us specific customer learning:

|Organization|Observed response|Proposed implementation|
|  ---  |  ---  |  ---  |
|Veridex|Invited an open testnet design partnership after declining a third-party testing budget.|One agreed testnet route and buyer adaptation; proposed $1,500 over five business days.|
|Nansen|After the internal referral, James declined pursuing the proposal in the October 12, 16:15:57 UTC decision.|Historical offer: read-only Ethereum Holdings data, Stellar testnet payment and source/operator handover; $2,400 over five business days.|
|CoCart|Founder Sébastien Dumont asked about introductions, the payer, referral compensation, responsibilities and contracting.|One customer’s headless cart, native WooCommerce checkout, payment/order operation and receiving; proposed $7,200 for 60 hours over fifteen business days.|
|Blockscout|Mojmir Racak expressed interest on October 12 and reported no current integration budget.|One approved PRO API token-information operation, buyer integration and handover; proposed $4,800 over ten business days.|


These are proposed workshares and observed conversations. The commissioning agreement and funded customer cohort remain to be selected. A source platform, its merchant operator and the customer funding implementation can be different organizations. CoCart’s questions, for example, require an explicit choice of the first merchant or agency and the commissioning arrangement. Bryce owns these relationships and subsequent agreements.

Each selected installation uses an original workorder naming the payer, merchant, independent buyer and receiving engineer. It defines the authorized source and access, exact operation, complete useful output, priced unit, host, receiving application and delivery acceptance. It also identifies the reason for a later purchase: a fresh period, changed source edition or distinct customer request. The same task then proceeds through installation, native payment, complete receiving, recurring use and handover.

The existing commercial model supports this adoption path: fixed-fee implementation of an agreed customer operation, followed by separately scoped care. A customer commissions the source and application adaptation; the merchant retains its resource receipts; TokenJunkieLabs invoices its agreed engineering and handover. Actual acceptance, implementation effort, corrections, support demand and collections inform following offers.

Stellar settles the operation the buyer approved. The approval binds the request to its network, asset, recipient and integer atomic amount. The native Stellar SDK and selected payment service verify and settle the authorization; the application connects that outcome to the original source, useful result and merchant fulfillment. Buyers retain signing and aggregate spending authority. Merchants retain control of their resources, terms and order actions.

We compose existing ecosystem infrastructure. The x402 Exact Stellar scheme and facilitator supply payment verification and settlement. Vellar’s optional discovery extension publishes eligible settled resources to its catalogue. OpenZeppelin, Veridex and Periplo supply relevant payment infrastructure, while Rumble Fish is developing facilitator, discovery and SDK capabilities. The existing MPP Charge workbench retains its own challenge, authorization and recovery model. The implementation uses existing SDKs and token contracts.

**Business and technical market comparison — October 12, 2026.** The closest products already make substantial parts of a paid Stellar service possible. The comparison below identifies the existing capability and the customer work our award must deliver around it.

|Existing product and current scope|Relationship to the proposed work|
|  ---  |  ---  |
|**ApiCharge.** Its [SCF-funded project](https://communityfund.stellar.org/project/apicharge-djv) combines desktop service publication and consumption with Soroban settlement and signed agreements preserving purchased access and quality of service. Its [current ML preview](https://apicharge.com/) deploys models as priced endpoints with typed inputs and customer-controlled infrastructure.|This is the closest comparison for merchant publication, pricing and customer access. Our funded deliverables install the selected customers’ source and receiving workflows: the analyst reviews the original material, acquires the complete agreed output, continues its editable business task and transfers the working installation to another maintainer.|
|**Nirium.** The maintained [SDK repository](https://github.com/nirium-protocol/nirium) provides TypeScript and Python clients, MCP and CLI interfaces, buyer-side x402 payment and `x402Serve()` seller middleware. Treasury and audit capabilities extend that platform.|Existing SDKs and facilitator integrations supply the payment foundation. Our package acceptance is the customer’s full source-to-result operation, including its application mappings, aggregate purchase state, interrupted delivery and installed response. Compatibility is assessed against each selected service’s actual scheme and terms.|
|**MPP Router and its Stellar agent wallet.** The [published wallet client](https://github.com/mpprouter/stellar-agent-wallet-skill) discovers services, pays x402 or MPP-gated calls with Stellar USDC and checks expected recipients and amounts. The [router workflow](https://www.mpprouter.dev/how-it-works) connects service discovery to a paid request.|Discovery and paid API access are established options. The proposed installation additionally defines what a complete customer job contains, retains every required result and source edition, and opens that output in the customer’s existing application. A later reporting period or source revision supplies a distinct useful purchase.|
|**Stellar Raven.** SDF’s [remote MCP service](https://raven.stellar.org/docs) combines searchable operations, executable service composition, official Stellar documentation and identified community information sources.|This supports developer research and integration. Our awarded deliverable is the operated merchant/buyer service, its customer data and its receiving maintainer. The original source and payment authority remain explicit throughout that installation.|


**Business value and adoption.** The first customer is an organization commissioning a repeatable information or application operation: for example, a complete filing comparison, reviewed laboratory delivery or recurring economic report. Its workorder names the commissioning payer, resource merchant, independent buyer and receiving engineer, with one agreed output and acceptance procedure. TokenJunkieLabs earns the fixed implementation fee and separately scoped care; the merchant retains its resource receipts. Selection favors a real reason for repeat use, an authorized source, a customer application that can receive the result and a maintainer who can operate the installation. The existing conversation records and delivery examples inform that selection.

**Technical improvement to be delivered.** The reusable product joins the original source, approved request and terms, native transfer, complete usable result and required fulfillment in one continuing customer operation. For a paginated dataset that includes its whole selected population; for a file or report it includes the complete bytes and the source edition used to produce them. An interrupted request reopens with its original financial and delivery state. Another authorized engineer receives the working configuration, decisions, history and customer files and completes the same task on the receiving host.

The six funded packages apply that architecture to the selected customers. T1 completes both source/application adaptations and a second operator’s handover. T2 operates the same useful service through two facilitators and completes the installed recovery cases. T3 establishes recurring mainnet use, restores the production state and completes independent maintenance. These are the proposed improvements reviewers can evaluate: useful customer output, repeat independent purchases, preserved operation when the payment provider changes and an installation another engineer can maintain.

**Open Track scope.** We selected Open Track for the merchant and buyer operating application and its reusable source-to-result workflow. It composes the existing x402 SDKs, payment services and facilitator catalogues. The funded improvement preserves source meaning and pagination, reviews exact requests and terms, acquires the complete result, receives it into the customer’s application or workbook, and reopens the service after interruption or on another authorized host. The six packages publish the adaptations required to operate that application across independently maintained services. Useful customer output, repeat purchases and successful receiving define the resulting ecosystem value. This application-level contribution and the business and technical comparison above explain the proposed [Open Track fit](https://stellar.gitbook.io/scf-handbook/scf-awards/build-award/open-track).

A retained comparison found 27 Vellar offers and two Periplo offers with no shared seller/route identity. The two-facilitator deliverable therefore includes actual registration and integration of the **same useful service** with both operators. Its completion must preserve the customer operation when payment infrastructure changes. Reusable integration, receiving and operating improvements return to the public source.

The system has six components: the merchant’s private source/release workspace; its public HTTP or MCP operation; the native Stellar SDK and facilitator; the buyer’s private approval and spending state; complete-result and delivery records; and merchant fulfillment/accounting. Node.js supplies merchant and buyer interfaces. Source adapters and receiving applications retain their own native data and operating semantics.

|Stage|Implemented behavior|
|  ---  |  ---  |
|Review and publish|The merchant selects a source edition or named live query, request schema, output, limits and resolved payment options. Review includes source rights, route, network, asset, recipient, amount and authorization lifetime. Source or terms changes become later reviewed states.|
|Connect the source|Adapters preserve types, missing and null values, pagination, keys, units, time basis and snapshot/live behavior. Customer-controlled credential or OAuth references select authorized access. The output identifies its source edition.|
|Approve and purchase|The buyer retains the endpoint, method or MCP tool, arguments, selected terms and scope. The remote schema and challenge must match before signing. Per-payment limits and the application’s existing reservation/budget owner govern spending.|
|Settle and deliver|The facilitator verifies and settles the native authorization. The application retains the server outcome, complete output and durable merchant notification. Independent RPC reconciliation checks the transaction’s network, asset, parties and atomic amount.|
|Use and continue|The receiving application opens all pages and files required by the task. A parent acquisition retains its priced requests and unfinished coverage. Earlier acquired output remains available when a later source edition changes.|
|Operate and hand over|The customer selects its release, HTTPS service, restricted administration and supervision. A receiving engineer can drain, restart, roll back and restore the installation with its operating history and complete customer files.|


**Recurring editorial data products.** The delivered WordPress merchant workspace turns a later source edition into a reviewable customer product. The operator saves an approved baseline as a refresh plan, continues the original native capture, inspects the complete source and projected changes, and approves the exact candidate before issuing its successor through the existing publisher. The same browser, CLI and agent interfaces preserve earlier acquired editions, original request identities and unfinished decisions when another engineer receives the workspace. This supplies a concrete recurring-use workflow for the selected customer installations. [Merged implementation and complete operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/1135e64cca2da5948c2d3e2c78119094d88f41d2/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/wordpress/REFRESH.md).

For paid MCP, the HTTP endpoint, tool and arguments are retained separately from the payment resource. An unsigned call obtains the challenge. Its full payment option, including authorization timeout, must match the saved quote before the buyer retains dispatch state and sends the signed call. The official MCP SDK carries payment and settlement metadata. HTTP operations use the native HTTP transport.

Recovery keeps server confirmation, independently observed transfer, complete output, receiver acknowledgment and fulfillment separately visible. An uncertain signed response stays attached to its original dispatch for reconciliation. Reopening an acquired result uses saved work; unfinished delivery continues from its original intent. A changed request or new purchase receives a new review.

Browser, terminal, typed clients and MCP operate the same retained workspaces. Customer exports include configuration selection, history and all referenced files. The receiving host supplies current authorized secret references. Buyer accounting also carries reviewed expense and credit allocations into connected QuickBooks and Xero accounts, with review of changed charts, affected mappings and journal lines before application.

The merchant's pricing workspace connects those operations to its customer offer. It retains the approved tariff and saved uniform quote, selects the actual usage period and counting basis, and compares their values with the recorded supplier-cost basis. The operator enters the monthly quantity for a proposed change, reviews the resulting native price, and carries the measured source into an ordinary customer quotation revision. The original pricing, scenario and Commercial workspaces retain the same requests and history. [Merged usage, pricing and quotation workflow](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/318).

The merchant financial workspace carries that paid operation into its original settlement accounting and customer records. An invoice can issue reviewed Stellar wallet terms; native receiving verifies the returned transfer and applies its original customer receipt. Issued service invoices retain exact amounts and billing identity; actual receipts, dated allocations and credits determine the balance. Reviewed installment plans distribute that balance across due dates and preserve every customer edition. The Xero handover maps issued invoices and credits to the receiving organisation's original templates, retains returned document IDs and exact amounts, and continues corrections through the same package family. Native network, asset and atomic amount remain attached to the original settlement; commercial valuations retain their explicit basis. The receiving engineer can reopen the complete workspace, customer files and financial history and continue the same task.

Acceptance operates two cases against the deployed service: an interrupted settled purchase and a merchant-delivery failure. Their records retain the actual notification and acknowledgment, financial and delivery outcomes, response and recovery times, material remediation or residual findings, and the receiving engineer’s same-case reopening after drain/restart. An uncertain payment is reconciled through its original intent. A coverage gap remains visible until observation resumes.

A completed purchase joins a distinct approved intent, an independently observed native transfer and complete useful output. Native transactions are counted once within each network. The cohort counts distinct accountable operator IDs whose reviewed deployment identifies an independent operator or customer, its buyer or merchant role, source basis, required network and operating or handed-over state. An operator’s agents and wallets share that identity; they do not create additional independent buyers. These are source-supported operator declarations, not automatic verification of corporate independence. Team-operated development purchases do not qualify. A returning buyer completes distinct intent groups on at least two UTC days. Reopening an acquired result or resuming its download continues the original purchase. Facilitators are also deduplicated by accountable operator for the same useful operation. For each installation, we record the customer’s existing task and, where available, its prior active effort, manual corrections and time to useful output. Comparison uses the same input/output definition and source population or period. For the merchant's pricing work, we also record the active effort needed to reconcile usage, review the current price and prepare the next customer quote. The saved comparison retains its quantity, period, counting basis and supplier-cost coverage; collections come from the original payment and accounting records.
